text:
Luca (finance): Quick flag 10 AcmeMarket (FR) bought Redwood seats through a marketplace integration. Customer invoices show VAT charged at FR rate but marketplace claims OSS should handle VAT. Which path do we take?
Anya (product ops): Marketplace integration notes: partner collects payments and sends us net settlement. Their docs say they handle VAT under OSS on our behalf. But contract with partner is blurry.
Mei (billing): Our billing system received a settlement CSV showing gross vs net: partner withheld 20% VAT (France 20%) and remitted to tax authority. They sent us a net pay of the item price minus VAT. We recorded revenue net of VAT.
Tom (legal): Need to confirm: are we registered in OSS for EU supplies? If we are, we can opt for OSS and let marketplace settle VAT. If not, marketplace might be acting as deemed supplier under EU rules (marketplace facilitator).
Omar (sales): Customer says they saw VAT on their receipt and want a vendor invoice from Redwood showing VAT reversed. They're confused because the partner receipt shows VAT too.
TaxBot: Quick note  EU OSS vs marketplace split: if a marketplace is the deemed supplier (per recent VAT rules), the marketplace is liable for VAT. Otherwise the underlying supplier (Redwood) is liable. Verify contractual flow and who appears on the consumer-facing invoice.
Luca (finance): Action items: 1) Mei to pull settlement record and partner invoice; 2) Anya to share marketplace agreement clause on VAT/OSS; 3) Tom to confirm legal position on deemed supplier for FR sales.
Mei (billing): Pulled files: settlement_2024-06-30.csv + partner_invoice_6789.pdf. Partner invoice lists "VAT collected under OSS FR" and shows partner as supplier on the invoice. Our B2B invoice system still has Redwood as supplier for direct customers.
Anya (product ops): Marketplace API shows "seller_display_name: Redwood Inference" and "collected_vat: true". So UX shows Redwood but partner collects payment. That is a red flag for tax: display name alone doesn't determine supplier.
Tom (legal): If partner invoice displays themselves as supplier and they remit VAT via OSS, likely they're the deemed supplier. We need to check the Marketplace Agreement: look for clause "VAT collection" and "deemed supplier" language. If partner claims OSS remittance, get evidence of their OSS registration number.
TaxBot: Also check the EU place-of-supply rules: supplies of digital services to consumers are taxed where the consumer is located. So merchant/marketplace must apply correct VAT rate.
Mei (billing): Customer is consumer in FR. Partner applied 20% VAT and remitted. They sent us net settlement for seats sold through marketplace. Our invoice to partner is for the gross amount or the net? Partner invoiced us for the commission fee only. We haven't invoiced the end-customer.
Luca (finance): For revenue recognition: we booked net settlement as revenue because partner acted as principal for B2C. But we must be sure. If Redwood is principal, we should have charged VAT and partner incorrectly kept VAT.
Omar (sales): Customer emailed complaining to Redwood because they thought Redwood charged VAT. We need a customer-facing explanation.
Tom (legal): Draft reply: "The marketplace partner acted as the collecting party and remitted VAT on the sale under OSS. Redwood received a net settlement. We will share partner invoice and remittance evidence if you need it." But only send once partner confirms OSS filings.
Anya (product ops): I can ask partner to provide their OSS registration and a remittance report for the period. Also ask for copies of consumer-facing receipts showing partner as supplier.
Mei (billing): Uploading partner docs to tax_evidence/marketplace/partner_6789. Also tagging the transaction in billing system as MARKETPLACE_SETTLEMENT_PENDING_PROOF.
Luca (finance): If partner can't prove OSS remittance or if agreement says Redwood is supplier for VAT purposes, we'll need to reclaim VAT from partner or correct our invoices. That could be messy. Hold any refunds until resolved.
TaxBot: Reminder: maintain audit trail: settlement csv + partner invoice + customer receipt + partner OSS evidence. If partner is the deemed supplier, we should not be reporting VAT for these B2C sales.
Tom (legal): I'll review the marketplace agreement and draft a short clause request for partner to confirm OSS registration and that they are the VAT remitter for that settlement. If they refuse, we escalate to commercial.
Omar (sales): Customer reply template ready: short apology + explanation that we're investigating and will provide evidence of VAT remittance.
Mei (billing): Partner replied: "We collect and remit VAT under OSS; attached report for June and OSS-registration FR-OSS-4321.pdf". Sending to legal and finance.
Tom (legal): Reviewing partner OSS registration  looks valid. OK to respond to customer that partner remitted VAT. Save docs and close.
Luca (finance): Closing loop: adjust revenue tag to MARKETPLACE_PRINCIPAL for accounting and note VAT remitted by partner. Mei, attach docs to the ledger entry.
Mei (billing): Done. Customer informed. Thread closed. :white_check_mark:
